newsitem.title: UK: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, June 30.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, June 30.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Monday.

LONDON - Shares ended near the day's lows as sentiment was knocked by growing fears of interest rate rises and nervousness ahead of the Labour government's first budget on Wednesday. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,604.6, down 35.7 points, or 0.77 percent.

FRANKFURT - Shares lost steam, dragged lower in late trade by a weak start on Wall Street as the momentum that drove prices to new records last week wore off amid low turnover. The DAX-30 index closed at 3,785.77, down 9.64 points, or 0.25 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 3.766.89, down 43.03 points, or 1.13 percent.

PARIS - Shares slid lower to close just over one percent down, as softer Wall Street and bonds extended the Paris market's consolidation, traders said. The CAC-40 index closed at 2,858.26, down 32.78 points, or 1.13 percent.

ZURICH - Shares ended 1.4 percent lower, pushing the Swiss Market Index (SMI) below the 5,700 point level and ending a three-day record run. The Swiss market index closed at 5,620.6, down 79.7 points, or 1.40 percent.

MILAN - Shares closed lower across the board, weakened by a wave of profit-taking brought on partly by the softer trend on Wall Street as U.S. treasury bonds beat a fast retreat. The All Share Mibtel index closed at 13,182, down 206 points, or 1.54 percent.

AMSTERDAM - Shares closed one percent lower, backing away from an all-time high early in the session, after a batch of U.S. economic figures spooked Wall Street ahead of Fed policy meetings this week. The AEX index closed at 861.55, down 8.90 points, or 1.02 percent.

TOKYO - Stocks ended higher as robust demand erased losses brought on by a report that a corporate racketeer told prosecutors that Nikko Securities Co Ltd and Daiwa Securities Co Ltd conducted illegal stock deals for him, brokers said. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,604.96, up 81.21 points, or 0.40 percent.

HONG KONG - The stock market is closed from Monday to Wednesday as Hong Kong celebrates its return to Chinese rule on July 1. When it reopens on Thursday, the new era under China is expected to usher in a flood of Chinese money.

JOHANNESBURG - Bullion's slide to its weakest level in over four years winded South African gold shares, tearing three percent off the index at the close and wounding marginal mines specialist Randgold. The All-share index closed at 7,420.0, up 9.0 points, or 0.12 percent. The All Gold index closed at 965.0, down 29.8 points, or 0.49 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 8,790.5, up 42.9 points, or 3.00 percent.
